title: Tested USB audio results
text: First, these are preserved live USB speaker-to-microphone tests, not simulations. The fastest clean physical-path run delivered 8,131 payload bits per second using 8 P S K, rate-one-half coding, F F T 256, and a 1.5-to-15-kilohertz band.
evidence: The data-backed viewer loaded the recorded USB results and displayed 8,131 bit/s as the fastest validated run.

title: Bandwidth and reliability tradeoffs
text: The comparison also records failures. Wider bands and weaker coding were not consistently better: Q P S K rate two-thirds failed in one wide profile, while 8 P S K rate two-thirds became marginal. The reliable 8 P S K result retained rate-one-half forward error correction.
evidence: The viewer displayed the stored failed and marginal USB test outcomes beside the successful throughput bars.

title: Sustained FPGA loopback
text: For the raw hardware path, I sent 1,048,576 deterministic samples in 2,048 frames. Every sample returned byte-exact. The P L is paced at 250,000 samples per second; sustained host throughput measured 148,498 after fixed 512-sample Linux and D M A transaction overhead.
evidence: The results viewer showed the million-sample byte-exact benchmark and the completed 16 KiB modem loopback.

title: Live Cora end-to-end result
text: Here is the live Cora dashboard retaining the longest peak-setting run: 16,384 bytes, 43 of 43 packets, zero retries, zero packet errors, and a matching source and receive S H A 256. Useful payload throughput was 3.01 kilobits per second.
evidence: The actual board dashboard reported COMPLETE, 43/43 packets, 3.01 kbit/s, zero errors and 8PSK R1/2.

title: 250 ksps at 30 kHz
text: The water numbers are an engineering projection, not a benchmark. Assuming a transducer chain that truly passes 20 to 40 kilohertz, F F T 1024 and a 256-sample prefix, expected validated payload spans about 7 to 18 kilobits per second across the three profiles.
evidence: The projection view visibly labeled the numbers as estimates and displayed assumptions, body ceilings, and payload ranges.

title: Practical first-water target
text: I would plan the first field trial around 5 to 12 kilobits per second using Q P S K rate one-half and adaptive carriers. At 30 kilohertz, absorption is about 8.3 decibels per kilometer, and one meter per second of motion creates roughly 20 hertz of Doppler shift.
evidence: The viewer displayed the recommended 5–12 kbit/s field target and the absorption, Doppler, multipath, and bandwidth caveats.
